descriptions.summary: One model step's response within a turn. A single prompt can produce several, for example one per round of tool calls; a step that failed keeps its message, with Error set and any partial content.
descriptions.reason: Builders read one assistant message as the whole answer; upstream starts a new assistant message per model step (core/src/session/runner/step.ts).

descriptions.summary: Why the step ended: stop, length, tool-calls, content-filter, error or unknown; null while the step is still running.
descriptions.remarks: A step that failed reports error, or content-filter when the provider blocked the response.
descriptions.reason: Upstream normalises the provider's finish reason in session.step.ended and session.step.failed (core/src/session/message-updater.ts).

descriptions.summary: The provider's own finish-reason string, kept verbatim for diagnostics; it may be null. Use Finish for logic.
descriptions.reason: Upstream copies the provider's stop reason unnormalised beside Finish.

descriptions.summary: Set when this step failed, for example a provider error, a content filter or an interruption; the message and its partial content stay in the session.
descriptions.remarks: It is cleared when the step starts again on this same message. When a failure after partial output continues the turn, the continuation is a new message and this one keeps its error.
descriptions.reason: Builders could not tell a failed turn from a finished one; upstream sets it from session.step.failed and clears it on a retried step.started.

descriptions.summary: Set while a retry of this step is scheduled after a retryable provider error: the attempt number (the first retry is 2), when it runs, and the error that caused it.
descriptions.remarks: It is cleared when the retry starts or the session goes idle.
descriptions.reason: Upstream sets it from session.retry.scheduled (core/src/session/runner/retry.ts).

descriptions.summary: The step's output parts in the order they streamed: text, reasoning and tool calls.
descriptions.reason: The part order is the stream order upstream records.

descriptions.summary: The cost in US dollars of this step alone, computed by the server from the model's configured prices; null until the step finishes, and it may stay null when the step fails.
descriptions.reason: Builders summed it as a turn total; upstream computes it per step (core/src/session/runner/step.ts).

descriptions.summary: The token usage of this step alone; null until the step finishes, and it may stay null when the step fails.
descriptions.reason: Per-step usage, as Cost.

descriptions.summary: A live fragment of assistant text: append its Data.Delta to the text part its Data.AssistantMessageId and Data.Ordinal name.
descriptions.remarks: Deltas are never stored or replayed; after reconnecting, rely on SessionTextEnded or the session's messages.
descriptions.reason: Builders kept only deltas and lost text across reconnects; upstream declares stream fragments live-only (schema/src/session-event.ts).

descriptions.summary: The new text to append; it may batch several provider chunks.
descriptions.reason: Upstream batches deltas about every 100 ms.

descriptions.summary: The zero-based index of this text part among the text parts of its assistant message; the started, delta and ended events of one part share it.
descriptions.reason: Builders took it for a global sequence number.

descriptions.summary: The end of one assistant text part. It is durable and replayed, and its Data.Text holds the part's complete final text.
descriptions.reason: Upstream declares Text.Ended the replayable full-value boundary (schema/src/session-event.ts).

descriptions.summary: The complete text of the part; it replaces whatever was built up from deltas.
descriptions.reason: Upstream replaces the part's text with it.

descriptions.summary: Opaque provider metadata for the part, kept so it can be sent back to the provider; do not interpret it.
descriptions.reason: Upstream stores it for later provider requests only.

descriptions.summary: A prompt for the session's inbox. The call returns as soon as the prompt is stored, before the model runs; follow the turn on the event bus or with the experimental wait.
descriptions.reason: Builders awaited PromptAsync as if it returned the answer; upstream admits the input and schedules the run (protocol/src/groups/session.ts).

descriptions.summary: An optional message id of your own, starting with msg_, which makes the call idempotent: resending it returns the stored item and ignores the new content.
descriptions.remarks: An id that belongs to another session or another kind of record is a conflict (409).
descriptions.reason: Upstream's inbox admits an id once (core/src/session/inbox.ts).

descriptions.summary: Attachments as data: URIs, or file: URIs on the server's own file system, read when the prompt is submitted; at most 20 MiB each.
descriptions.reason: Builders sent client-side paths; upstream reads file: URIs on the server (core/src/session/prompt.ts).

descriptions.summary: Skills to attach by id; the server puts each skill's text before the prompt, and an unknown id is refused (400).
descriptions.reason: Upstream resolves skills by id at submission.

descriptions.summary: Steer, the default, puts the prompt into the running turn at its next step; Queue waits for the current turn to end and starts a new turn with it.
descriptions.reason: Upstream's inbox delivery modes (core/src/session/inbox.ts).

descriptions.summary: False stores the prompt without waking the session for it: an idle session leaves it pending until something else wakes it, while a session already running can still take it at its next boundary. The default is true.
descriptions.reason: Upstream skips scheduling the run when resume is false.

descriptions.summary: A new session, or, when Id names an existing one, that session returned unchanged.
descriptions.reason: Upstream's create is idempotent on the id (core/src/session.ts).

descriptions.summary: An optional session id of your own; when a session with it exists, that session is returned and the other members are ignored.
descriptions.reason: As the type summary.

descriptions.summary: Makes this a child session, such as a subagent's, of an existing parent. The child always works in the parent's location and inherits its metadata and permissions unless you set them.
descriptions.remarks: Agent and model are not inherited.
descriptions.reason: Upstream's create handler drops the location of a child and copies the parent's (server/src/handlers/session.ts).

descriptions.summary: The agent to use. When it is absent, the server chooses its default agent each time the session runs a step.
descriptions.reason: Upstream stores no agent when none is given (core/src/agent.ts).

descriptions.summary: The model to use. When it is absent, the server chooses its default model each time the session runs a step; an unavailable model is reported only when the session runs.
descriptions.reason: Builders expected create to validate the model; upstream resolves it per turn (core/src/session/runner/model.ts).

descriptions.summary: The directory the session works in; the server's working directory when absent. It is ignored when ParentId is set.
descriptions.reason: Upstream defaults to the process directory and gives a child its parent's location.

descriptions.summary: Session permission rules, checked after the agent's own; the last rule that matches wins, so they override the agent. Anything no rule matches asks.
descriptions.reason: Upstream appends session rules after the agent's (core/src/permission.ts).

descriptions.summary: The server began working on the session after it was woken while idle. When that work settles, exactly one of SessionExecutionSucceeded, SessionExecutionFailed or SessionExecutionInterrupted follows, however many prompts arrive meanwhile; a server that crashes mid-work publishes none.
descriptions.reason: Upstream publishes one terminal observation per busy period (core/src/session/execution.ts).

descriptions.summary: The execution finished the work it took on and the session went idle. Prompts it did not take, such as queued ones, can still be pending.
descriptions.reason: The turn-ending event builders need to wait on.

descriptions.summary: The session stopped on an error and went idle; its Data.Error says why.
descriptions.remarks: It is also published when a turn interrupted by repeated restarts can no longer be resumed.
descriptions.reason: Upstream publishes it from the run coordinator and from restart recovery (core/src/session/execution/restart.ts).

descriptions.summary: The session's work stopped before it finished; its Data.Reason says why.
descriptions.remarks: With the shutdown reason the turn is not over: the server keeps it marked in progress, and a server that resumes work after it restarts picks it up again with a new SessionExecutionStarted. A turn that cannot be resumed, or has been resumed too often, ends with SessionExecutionFailed.
descriptions.reason: Builders treated every interrupt as the end of a turn; upstream resumes a shutdown interrupt (core/src/session/execution/restart.ts).

descriptions.summary: The program to run, an executable rather than a command line. When it is absent the server picks a shell: the configured shell, then $SHELL, then a per-platform fallback.
descriptions.remarks: The fallback is, on Windows, the first of pwsh, powershell and Git Bash that is found, otherwise %COMSPEC%, or cmd.exe when COMSPEC is unset; /bin/zsh on macOS; and bash on PATH, or else /bin/sh, elsewhere. A configured shell that is not executable skips $SHELL and goes straight to the fallback. PowerShell starts with no added arguments, so its profile loads; pass -NoProfile in Args for a clean one.
descriptions.reason: Builders could not predict which shell a PTY gets; upstream's resolver order (core/src/pty.ts, core/src/shell/select.ts).

descriptions.summary: Arguments passed as they are to the program, with no shell parsing.
descriptions.remarks: When the program is bash, dash, fish, ksh, sh or zsh, the server appends -l after these arguments, so bash -c "cmd" receives -l as $0; the returned info shows it.
descriptions.reason: Upstream appends the login flag for login shells (core/src/pty.ts).

descriptions.summary: The start of the range, inclusive, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Unset, the range starts at the earliest message.
descriptions.reason: The wire says only 'from'; upstream compares it with message times in epoch milliseconds and treats it as inclusive (core/src/session/stats.ts).

descriptions.summary: The end of the range, exclusive, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Unset, the range ends now.
descriptions.reason: The wire says only 'to'; upstream compares it with message times in epoch milliseconds, defaults it to Date.now() and treats it as exclusive (core/src/session/stats.ts).

sessionScopedEvent.reason: Upstream routes every session-scoped event by data.sessionID; IEvent carries no common session id, so routing needs the id on the event itself.

event.reason: The global event bus is its own family surface; no per-id operations exist.

session.reason: The session is the SDK's primary working object: two dozen operations chain on one sessionID (ADR-0019); its upstream experimental routes, today session.log, carry OPENCODE003.

shell.reason: A shell is a live process worked over its id: get, remove and output share the shell working object (ADR-0019).

integration.reason: The connect and oauth flows are multi-step conversations with one integration; ten operations chain on integrationID (ADR-0019).

mcp.reason: MCP inventory and resource catalog form a flat client; experimental lifecycle operations take the server identifier explicitly on ExperimentalClient.

pty.reason: A pty is a live terminal worked over its id; the pinned surface adds update and connect operations to the trio (ADR-0019). Every public door of the family is hand-written over these raw clients because the WebSocket session and the connect-token handshake need knowledge generation may not import (ADR-0021).

persistentPty.reason: A persistent terminal is a live daemon-owned process worked over its id: get, update, snapshot, remove, connect-token, and the WebSocket connect chain on ptyID (ADR-0019); the session-keyed list, create, and read and the bare handoff and shutdown stay on the collection client with their route values as arguments, exactly as upstream flattens the group with sessionID as an input field. Every public door of the family is hand-written over these raw clients because the connect-token handshake and the WebSocket session need knowledge generation may not import (ADR-0021, extended to this family); its upstream experimental routes carry OPENCODE002.

agent.reason: agent.get is the family's only per-id operation; a single lookup takes the id as an argument (ADR-0019).

credential.reason: Update and remove are single-shot admin actions; the id rides as an argument (ADR-0019).

permission.reason: saved.remove is the family's only per-id operation; the pending-request surface lives on sessions (ADR-0019).

provider.reason: provider.get is the family's only per-id operation; a single lookup takes the id as an argument (ADR-0019).

websearch.reason: Query and provider listing carry no per-id operations; a mass-noun container names the domain.

command.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

debug.reason: Diagnostic actions carry no per-id operations; a mass-noun container names the surface (ADR-0019).

experimental.reason: Experimental operations share a flat client that flags their stability; route identifiers are explicit method arguments rather than session handles, and its upstream experimental routes carry OPENCODE001.

model.reason: The Models folder and namespace belong to the generated model layer; LanguageModels names the provider model catalog without shadowing either (ADR-0019 flat).

plugin.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

project.reason: Project update is a single-shot admin action with an explicit id; list has no per-id operation (ADR-0019).

reference.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

skill.reason: The family carries no per-id operations; a flat container holds its calls (ADR-0019).

vcs.reason: The initialism does not pluralize; the mass-noun container names the domain (ADR-0019).

location.reason: Location resolution is a cross-cutting utility and belongs on the root client.

server.reason: Status and server lifecycle operations form one server-scoped surface; the singular client exposes the server info as GetInfoAsync.

worktree.reason: The family's full pinned surface (list, create, remove, refresh) names its project through a required projectID and carries no required path id, so ADR-0019 yields a flat client. The whole surface is selected and retains the upstream worktree terminology.

form.reason: form.list is the family's entire pinned surface (unlike session.form.*, a distinct group that rides the session working object): a bare GET with no id in its path, so it carries no per-id operations, ever, and a flat container holds its one call (ADR-0019).

fs.reason: The three fs operations (list, find, read) carry no per-id operation, so a flat container holds the calls (ADR-0019); the client is named for the upstream tag and the FileSystem.Entry component, not the abbreviation.

rpc.reason: rpc.call is the family's only pinned operation and its two route values (rpcID, method) ride as arguments, exactly like agent.get and provider.get (ADR-0019); the initialism does not pluralize, so the flat container keeps the domain name, exactly like vcs.

config.reason: config.shells is the family's entire selected surface and carries no per-id operations; configuration reading (config.get) remains declined at the structural-union wall, and the configuration patch is experimental.config.update on the experimental family.
